1	"""Instants, half-open intervals, and the interval algebra the spec requires.
2	
3	The spec's temporal rules are the reason this module exists rather than bare
4	``datetime`` use: a local wall time plus an IANA zone is not always a single
5	instant, and the two cases where it is not must be refused rather than guessed.
6	Elapsed duration is always computed in UTC; zones are retained for rendering.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
12	from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
13	from typing import Iterable, Sequence
14	from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
15	
16	__all__ = [
17	    "AmbiguousLocalTime",
18	    "Interval",
19	    "InvalidInterval",
20	    "LocalTime",
21	    "NonexistentLocalTime",
22	    "TemporalError",
23	    "merge",
24	    "subtract",
25	    "total_duration",
26	]
27	
28	
29	class TemporalError(ValueError):
30	    """Base class for a local time or interval that cannot be trusted."""
31	
32	
33	class NonexistentLocalTime(TemporalError):
34	    """The wall time never occurs in that zone (spring-forward gap)."""
35	
36	
37	class AmbiguousLocalTime(TemporalError):
38	    """The wall time occurs twice in that zone and no fold was supplied."""
39	
40	
41	class InvalidInterval(TemporalError):
42	    """An interval whose end does not strictly follow its start."""
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class LocalTime:
47	    """A wall time entered by staff, kept alongside the zone it was entered in.
48	
49	    ``fold`` is only meaningful for a repeated wall time: 0 selects the first
50	    occurrence (before the clocks go back), 1 the second. Supplying it for an
51	    unambiguous time is harmless and ignored.
52	    """
53	
54	    wall: str
55	    zone: str
56	    fold: int | None = None
57	
58	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
59	        naive = datetime.fromisoformat(self.wall)
60	        if naive.tzinfo is not None:
61	            raise TemporalError(
62	                f"{self.wall!r} already carries an offset; pass a bare wall time "
63	                "and an IANA zone so the entered local context is preserved"
64	            )
65	        tz = ZoneInfo(self.zone)
66	
67	        # A gap is detected by round-tripping: for a time that never occurred,
68	        # zoneinfo silently shifts it, so the return trip lands somewhere else.
69	        probe = naive.replace(tzinfo=tz)
70	        if probe.astimezone(timezone.utc).astimezone(tz).replace(tzinfo=None) != naive:
71	            raise NonexistentLocalTime(
72	                f"{self.wall} does not occur in {self.zone}; clocks skip that hour"
73	            )
74	
75	        # A repeated time has two distinct offsets. zoneinfo would default to
76	        # fold=0 and quietly pick one, which the spec forbids.
77	        if probe.utcoffset() != naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=1).utcoffset():
78	            if self.fold is None:
79	                raise AmbiguousLocalTime(
80	                    f"{self.wall} occurs twice in {self.zone}; supply fold=0 or fold=1"
81	                )
82	
83	        object.__setattr__(self, "_naive", naive)
84	        object.__setattr__(self, "_tz", tz)
85	
86	    @property
87	    def instant(self) -> datetime:
88	        """The single UTC instant this wall time and zone denote."""
89	        naive: datetime = getattr(self, "_naive")
90	        tz: ZoneInfo = getattr(self, "_tz")
91	        return naive.replace(tzinfo=tz, fold=self.fold or 0).astimezone(timezone.utc)
92	
93	    def render(self, zone: str) -> str:
94	        """The same instant as wall time in another zone, for display only."""
95	        return self.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone)).isoformat()
96	
97	
98	@dataclass(frozen=True, order=True)
99	class Interval:
100	    """A half-open ``[start, end)`` span of UTC instants.
101	
102	    Half-open is what lets a 22:00 event and a 22:00 window sit adjacent
103	    without being reported as a conflict.
104	    """
105	
106	    start: datetime
107	    end: datetime
108	    # Provenance for rendering and export. Excluded from comparison so an
109	    # interval derived by merge/subtract still equals an equivalent entered one.
110	    start_zone: str | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
111	    end_zone: str | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
112	    start_fold: int | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
113	    end_fold: int | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
114	
115	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
116	        for name, value in (("start", self.start), ("end", self.end)):
117	            if value.tzinfo is None:
118	                raise InvalidInterval(f"{name} must be an aware instant, got {value!r}")
119	        object.__setattr__(self, "start", self.start.astimezone(timezone.utc))
120	        object.__setattr__(self, "end", self.end.astimezone(timezone.utc))
121	        if self.end <= self.start:
122	            raise InvalidInterval(
123	                f"end {self.end.isoformat()} does not follow start {self.start.isoformat()}"
124	            )
125	
126	    @classmethod
127	    def of(
128	        cls,
129	        start_wall: str,
130	        end_wall: str,
131	        zone: str,
132	        end_zone: str | None = None,
133	        start_fold: int | None = None,
134	        end_fold: int | None = None,
135	    ) -> "Interval":
136	        """Build from entered wall times. ``end_zone`` differs for travel legs."""
137	        arrival_zone = end_zone or zone
138	        return cls(
139	            LocalTime(start_wall, zone, start_fold).instant,
140	            LocalTime(end_wall, arrival_zone, end_fold).instant,
141	            start_zone=zone,
142	            end_zone=arrival_zone,
143	            start_fold=start_fold,
144	            end_fold=end_fold,
145	        )
146	
147	    def wall(self, which: str = "start") -> str:
148	        """The entered wall time, rendered back in the zone it was entered in."""
149	        instant = self.start if which == "start" else self.end
150	        zone = self.start_zone if which == "start" else self.end_zone
151	        if zone is None:
152	            return instant.isoformat()
153	        return instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone)).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M")
154	
155	    @property
156	    def duration(self) -> timedelta:
157	        return self.end - self.start
158	
159	    def overlaps(self, other: "Interval") -> bool:
160	        return self.start < other.end and other.start < self.end
161	
162	    def intersect(self, other: "Interval") -> "Interval | None":
163	        start = max(self.start, other.start)
164	        end = min(self.end, other.end)
165	        return Interval(start, end) if start < end else None
166	
167	    def render(self, zone: str) -> str:
168	        tz = ZoneInfo(zone)
169	        return f"{self.start.astimezone(tz):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}-{self.end.astimezone(tz):%H:%M}"
170	
171	
172	def merge(intervals: Iterable[Interval]) -> list[Interval]:
173	    """Union overlapping or touching intervals so shared time is counted once."""
174	    ordered = sorted(intervals, key=lambda i: (i.start, i.end))
175	    merged: list[Interval] = []
176	    for current in ordered:
177	        if merged and current.start <= merged[-1].end:
178	            previous = merged[-1]
179	            if current.end > previous.end:
180	                merged[-1] = Interval(previous.start, current.end)
181	        else:
182	            merged.append(current)
183	    return merged
184	
185	
186	def subtract(interval: Interval, blockers: Sequence[Interval]) -> list[Interval]:
187	    """What remains of ``interval`` once every blocker is removed."""
188	    remainder = [interval]
189	    for blocker in merge(blockers):
190	        next_remainder: list[Interval] = []
191	        for piece in remainder:
192	            if not piece.overlaps(blocker):
193	                next_remainder.append(piece)
194	                continue
195	            if piece.start < blocker.start:
196	                next_remainder.append(Interval(piece.start, blocker.start))
197	            if blocker.end < piece.end:
198	                next_remainder.append(Interval(blocker.end, piece.end))
199	        remainder = next_remainder
200	    return remainder
201	
202	
203	def total_duration(intervals: Iterable[Interval]) -> timedelta:
204	    """Summed duration after union, so overlapping windows never double count."""
205	    return sum((i.duration for i in merge(intervals)), timedelta())

"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1's late-return comparison actually uses. The
spec's AthleteProfile, group membership, and scenario revisions are deliberately
absent: they depend on the unanswered question of whether the modelling unit is
a representative athlete, a subgroup, or an individual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin; ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed before an obligation
    starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is inferred.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None

    @property
    def mandatory(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind not in OPTIONAL_KINDS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    It is never inferred from free time. ``kind`` records where the opportunity
    sits (hotel, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

    id: str
    label: str
    interval: Interval
    kind: str = "hotel"
    proposed: bool = False


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """A named plan: obligations, entered sleep windows, and its assumptions."""

    id: str
    title: str
    display_zone: str
    events: list[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
    windows: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = field(default_factory=list)
    assumptions: AssumptionSet | None = None

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.mandatory]

2	
3	This implements steps 1-8 of the spec's opportunity calculation. The two rules
4	worth restating, because every future change will be tempted to break them:
5	
6	* Free time is not opportunity. Only an entered or proposed window counts.
7	* Opportunity is not sleep. Nothing here estimates sleep obtained, and the
8	  report names its own measure so a caller cannot mistake it for one.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
14	from datetime import timedelta
15	
16	from .schedule import Event, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
17	from .temporal import Interval, merge, subtract, total_duration
18	
19	__all__ = ["Comparison", "Conflict", "EventChange", "OpportunityReport", "compare", "evaluate"]
20	
21	MEASURE = "sleep opportunity"
22	
23	
24	def _hours(delta: timedelta) -> float:
25	    return round(delta.total_seconds() / 3600, 6)
26	
27	
28	@dataclass(frozen=True)
29	class Conflict:
30	    """An obligation that overlaps an entered sleep window.
31	
32	    Reported, never resolved by deletion: the treatment stays on the schedule
33	    and the staff decides.
34	    """
35	
36	    window_id: str
37	    event_id: str
38	    event_kind: str
39	    overlap: Interval
40	
41	    def describe(self) -> str:
42	        return (
43	            f"{self.event_id} ({self.event_kind}) overlaps window {self.window_id} "
44	            f"for {_hours(self.overlap.duration)}h"
45	        )
46	
47	
48	@dataclass(frozen=True)
49	class OpportunityReport:
50	    """Opportunity within one reporting interval, with its provenance."""
51	
52	    scenario: Scenario
53	    reporting_interval: Interval
54	    feasible: list[Interval]
55	    sources: list[ProtectedSleepWindow]
56	    conflicts: list[Conflict]
57	    target_hours: float
58	    target_source: str
59	    measure: str = MEASURE
60	
61	    @property
62	    def hours(self) -> float:
63	        """Opportunity hours after union, so overlapping windows count once."""
64	        return _hours(total_duration(self.feasible))
65	
66	    @property
67	    def shortfall_hours(self) -> float:
68	        return round(max(0.0, self.target_hours - self.hours), 6)
69	
70	
71	@dataclass(frozen=True)
72	class EventChange:
73	    event_id: str
74	    shift: timedelta
75	
76	
77	@dataclass(frozen=True)
78	class Comparison:
79	    baseline: OpportunityReport
80	    candidate: OpportunityReport
81	    changed_events: list[EventChange] = field(default_factory=list)
82	    measure: str = MEASURE
83	
84	    @property
85	    def hours_delta(self) -> float:
86	        return round(self.candidate.hours - self.baseline.hours, 6)
87	
88	    @property
89	    def resolved_conflicts(self) -> list[Conflict]:
90	        candidate_keys = {(c.window_id, c.event_id) for c in self.candidate.conflicts}
91	        return [c for c in self.baseline.conflicts if (c.window_id, c.event_id) not in candidate_keys]
92	
93	
94	def _blocked_intervals(scenario: Scenario) -> list[Interval]:
95	    """Mandatory obligations widened by the assumed transitions around them."""
96	    assumptions = scenario.assumptions
97	    pre_bed = assumptions.pre_bed if assumptions else timedelta()
98	    morning = assumptions.morning if assumptions else timedelta()
99	    blocked = []
100	    for event in scenario.obligations():
101	        blocked.append(
102	            Interval(event.interval.start - morning, event.interval.end + pre_bed)
103	        )
104	    return merge(blocked)
105	
106	
107	def evaluate(scenario: Scenario, reporting_interval: Interval) -> OpportunityReport:
108	    """Opportunity for ``scenario`` inside ``reporting_interval``.
109	
110	    The reporting interval is supplied rather than derived so that an overnight
111	    total and a 24-hour total are two explicit calls, never one blended number.
112	    """
113	    if scenario.assumptions is None:
114	        raise ValueError("scenario needs an AssumptionSet before it can be evaluated")
115	
116	    blocked = _blocked_intervals(scenario)
117	
118	    conflicts: list[Conflict] = []
119	    feasible: list[Interval] = []
120	    sources: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = []
121	
122	    for window in scenario.windows:
123	        clipped = window.interval.intersect(reporting_interval)
124	        if clipped is None:
125	            continue
126	        sources.append(window)
127	        for event in scenario.obligations():
128	            overlap = clipped.intersect(event.interval)
129	            if overlap is not None:
130	                conflicts.append(
131	                    Conflict(window.id, event.id, event.kind, overlap)
132	                )
133	        feasible.extend(subtract(clipped, blocked))
134	
135	    return OpportunityReport(
136	        scenario=scenario,
137	        reporting_interval=reporting_interval,
138	        feasible=merge(feasible),
139	        sources=sources,
140	        conflicts=conflicts,
141	        target_hours=scenario.assumptions.sleep_target_hours,
142	        target_source=scenario.assumptions.source,
143	    )
144	
145	
146	def _changed_events(baseline: Scenario, candidate: Scenario) -> list[EventChange]:
147	    before = {e.id: e for e in baseline.events}
148	    changes = []
149	    for event in candidate.events:
150	        original = before.get(event.id)
151	        if original and original.interval.start != event.interval.start:
152	            changes.append(
153	                EventChange(event.id, event.interval.start - original.interval.start)
154	            )
155	    return changes
156	
157	
158	def compare(baseline: OpportunityReport, candidate: OpportunityReport) -> Comparison:
159	    """Difference between two scenarios evaluated on common ground.
160	
161	    Refuses mismatched assumptions or reporting intervals: a difference in
162	    opportunity is only interpretable when everything else was held equal.
163	    """
164	    if baseline.scenario.assumptions != candidate.scenario.assumptions:
165	        raise ValueError(
166	            "cannot compare scenarios built on a different assumption set; "
167	            f"baseline target {baseline.target_hours}h from {baseline.target_source!r}, "
168	            f"candidate target {candidate.target_hours}h from {candidate.target_source!r}"
169	        )
170	    if baseline.reporting_interval != candidate.reporting_interval:
171	        raise ValueError("cannot compare reports covering different reporting intervals")
172	
173	    return Comparison(
174	        baseline=baseline,
175	        candidate=candidate,
176	        changed_events=_changed_events(baseline.scenario, candidate.scenario),
177	    )
178

1	"""JSON serialization for scenarios.
2	
3	Times are stored as the wall time and IANA zone they were *entered* in, not as
4	a normalised UTC stamp. That is what makes the round-trip lossless in the sense
5	the spec asks for: a flight entered as departing 21:30 Denver and arriving
6	23:40 Chicago comes back the same way, not as two Chicago timestamps.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import json
12	from pathlib import Path
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
16	from .temporal import Interval
17	
18	__all__ = [
19	    "load_scenario",
20	    "save_scenario",
21	    "scenario_from_dict",
22	    "scenario_to_dict",
23	]
24	
25	FORMAT_VERSION = 1
26	
27	
28	def _interval_to_dict(interval: Interval) -> dict[str, Any]:
29	    payload: dict[str, Any] = {
30	        "start": interval.wall("start"),
31	        "end": interval.wall("end"),
32	        "start_zone": interval.start_zone,
33	        "end_zone": interval.end_zone,
34	    }
35	    if interval.start_fold is not None:
36	        payload["start_fold"] = interval.start_fold
37	    if interval.end_fold is not None:
38	        payload["end_fold"] = interval.end_fold
39	    return payload
40	
41	
42	def _interval_from_dict(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> Interval:
43	    return Interval.of(
44	        payload["start"],
45	        payload["end"],
46	        payload["start_zone"],
47	        end_zone=payload.get("end_zone"),
48	        start_fold=payload.get("start_fold"),
49	        end_fold=payload.get("end_fold"),
50	    )
51	
52	
53	def scenario_to_dict(scenario: Scenario) -> dict[str, Any]:
54	    assumptions = scenario.assumptions
55	    return {
56	        "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
57	        "id": scenario.id,
58	        "title": scenario.title,
59	        "display_zone": scenario.display_zone,
60	        "assumptions": None
61	        if assumptions is None
62	        else {
63	            "sleep_target_hours": assumptions.sleep_target_hours,
64	            "pre_bed_minutes": assumptions.pre_bed_minutes,
65	            "morning_minutes": assumptions.morning_minutes,
66	            "source": assumptions.source,
67	        },
68	        "events": [
69	            {
70	                "id": e.id,
71	                "kind": e.kind,
72	                "title": e.title,
73	                "movable": e.movable,
74	                "location": e.location,
75	                "interval": _interval_to_dict(e.interval),
76	            }
77	            for e in scenario.events
78	        ],
79	        "windows": [
80	            {
81	                "id": w.id,
82	                "label": w.label,
83	                "kind": w.kind,
84	                "proposed": w.proposed,
85	                "interval": _interval_to_dict(w.interval),
86	            }
87	            for w in scenario.windows
88	        ],
89	    }
90	
91	
92	def scenario_from_dict(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> Scenario:
93	    version = payload.get("format_version")
94	    if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
95	        raise ValueError(
96	            f"unsupported scenario format_version {version!r}; expected {FORMAT_VERSION}"
97	        )
98	    raw_assumptions = payload.get("assumptions")
99	    return Scenario(
100	        id=payload["id"],
101	        title=payload["title"],
102	        display_zone=payload["display_zone"],
103	        events=[
104	            Event(
105	                id=e["id"],
106	                kind=e["kind"],

"""Compare two scenario files and print the difference in sleep opportunity.

Usage::

    python -m sleep_scheduler fixtures/late-return-baseline.json \\
                              fixtures/late-return-candidate.json

The wording here is deliberately constrained. The report says "opportunity",
names the source of its target, and prints the forecast status rather than a
forecast. It has no vocabulary for effectiveness, fatigue, or readiness,
because nothing in this codebase can compute them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from .adapter import get_adapter
from .opportunity import Comparison, compare, evaluate
from .persistence import load_scenario
from .schedule import Scenario
from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["default_reporting_interval", "main", "render_comparison"]


def default_reporting_interval(*scenarios: Scenario) -> Interval:
    """The full span the given scenarios cover.

    Derived rather than hardcoded: a fixed default silently reported zero
    opportunity for any scenario falling outside it. Pass ``--window`` to
    narrow this to a specific overnight or 24-hour interval, which is what the
    spec's separate overnight and 24-hour totals need.
    """
    intervals = [
        item.interval
        for scenario in scenarios
        for item in (*scenario.events, *scenario.windows)
    ]
    if not intervals:
        raise ValueError("scenario contains no events or sleep windows to report on")
    return Interval(
        min(i.start for i in intervals), max(i.end for i in intervals)
    )


def _hhmm(hours: float) -> str:
    total = round(hours * 60)
    return f"{total // 60}h {total % 60:02d}m"


def render_comparison(comparison: Comparison) -> str:
    baseline, candidate = comparison.baseline, comparison.candidate
    zone = candidate.scenario.display_zone
    lines: list[str] = []

    lines.append(f"Measure: {comparison.measure} (not sleep obtained)")
    lines.append(f"Reporting interval: {candidate.reporting_interval.render(zone)} {zone}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"{'Scenario':<44}{'Opportunity':>13}{'Shortfall':>12}")
    for report in (baseline, candidate):
        lines.append(
            f"{report.scenario.title:<44}{_hhmm(report.hours):>13}{_hhmm(report.shortfall_hours):>12}"
        )
    sign = "+" if comparison.hours_delta >= 0 else "-"
    lines.append(f"{'Difference':<44}{sign + _hhmm(abs(comparison.hours_delta)):>13}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"Target: {_hhmm(candidate.target_hours)} (source: {candidate.target_source})")
    assumptions = candidate.scenario.assumptions
    lines.append(
        f"Transitions assumed: {assumptions.pre_bed_minutes} min before sleep, "
        f"{assumptions.morning_minutes} min after waking"
    )
    lines.append("")

    if comparison.changed_events:
        lines.append("Changed events:")
        for change in comparison.changed_events:
            direction = "later" if change.shift.total_seconds() > 0 else "earlier"
            minutes = abs(int(change.shift.total_seconds() // 60))
            lines.append(f"  - {change.event_id}: moved {minutes // 60}h {minutes % 60:02d}m {direction}")
    else:
        lines.append("Changed events: none")
    lines.append("")

    for label, report in (("Baseline", baseline), ("Candidate", candidate)):
        if report.conflicts:
            lines.append(f"{label} conflicts (not resolved automatically):")
            for conflict in report.conflicts:
                lines.append(f"  - {conflict.describe()}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{label} conflicts: none")
    lines.append("")

    adapter = get_adapter()
    result = adapter.simulate(candidate)
    lines.append(f"Forecast ({result.adapter_name} v{result.adapter_version}): {result.reason}")
    for warning in adapter.validate(candidate):
        lines.append(f"  ! {warning}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="sleep_scheduler",
        description="Compare sleep opportunity between two scenario files.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("baseline", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("candidate", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--window",
        nargs=3,
        metavar=("START", "END", "ZONE"),
        default=None,
        help=(
            "reporting interval as two wall times and an IANA zone, e.g. "
            "--window 2026-09-12T18:00 2026-09-13T12:00 America/Chicago; "
            "defaults to the full span both scenarios cover"
        ),
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        baseline_scenario = load_scenario(args.baseline)
        candidate_scenario = load_scenario(args.candidate)
        if args.window:
            reporting = Interval.of(args.window[0], args.window[1], args.window[2])
        else:
            reporting = default_reporting_interval(baseline_scenario, candidate_scenario)
        baseline = evaluate(baseline_scenario, reporting)
        candidate = evaluate(candidate_scenario, reporting)
        comparison = compare(baseline, candidate)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot read {exc.filename}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    print(render_comparison(comparison))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

most are the negative ones: the report must never print a fatigue or

"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.cli import main, render_comparison
from sleep_scheduler.opportunity import compare, evaluate
from sleep_scheduler.persistence import load_scenario
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures"
CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
OVERNIGHT = Interval.of("2026-09-12T18:00", "2026-09-13T12:00", CHICAGO)


def fixture_comparison():
    baseline = evaluate(load_scenario(FIXTURES / "late-return-baseline.json"), OVERNIGHT)
    candidate = evaluate(load_scenario(FIXTURES / "late-return-candidate.json"), OVERNIGHT)
    return compare(baseline, candidate)


def test_moving_the_morning_lift_later_increases_opportunity():
    delta = fixture_comparison()
    assert delta.hours_delta > 0


def test_baseline_fixture_falls_short_of_the_assumed_target():
    delta = fixture_comparison()
    assert delta.baseline.shortfall_hours > 0


def test_rendered_report_labels_the_measure_as_opportunity():
    assert "sleep opportunity" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()


FORECAST_TERMS = ("effectiveness", "fatigue", "predicted sleep", "sleep obtained", "readiness")
NEGATIONS = ("no ", "not ", "unavailable", "cannot", "carry no")


def test_forecast_terms_appear_only_inside_an_explicit_denial():
    # These words are allowed in a sentence that says the value is unavailable,
    # and nowhere else. A line stating one as a result would fail here.
    for line in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower().splitlines():
        if any(term in line for term in FORECAST_TERMS):
            assert any(marker in line for marker in NEGATIONS), (
                f"line states a forecast term as a result: {line!r}"
            )


def test_report_opens_by_disclaiming_that_opportunity_is_sleep_obtained():
    first_line = render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).splitlines()[0].lower()
    assert "sleep opportunity" in first_line
    assert "not sleep obtained" in first_line


def test_numeric_result_rows_carry_no_forecast_terms():
    # The rows a reader takes numbers from must be opportunity-only.
    text = render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()
    rows = [l for l in text.splitlines() if "h " in l and ("late return" in l or "difference" in l)]
    assert rows, "expected the comparison table to have result rows"
    for row in rows:
        for forbidden in FORECAST_TERMS:
            assert forbidden not in row, f"result row must not mention {forbidden!r}: {row!r}"

    assert "staff default" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison())


def test_rendered_report_states_the_forecast_is_unavailable():
    assert "unavailable" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()

    assert "lift" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()

            str(FIXTURES / "late-return-baseline.json"),

    )
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert code == 0
    assert "sleep opportunity" in out.lower()

    """Same fixture, different dates, so a hardcoded window cannot match it."""
    import json

    payload = json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text())
    for group in ("events", "windows"):
        for item in payload[group]:
            for edge in ("start", "end"):
                item["interval"][edge] = item["interval"][edge].replace("2026-09-1", "2027-04-1")
    path = tmp_path / name
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload))

def test_default_reporting_window_covers_a_scenario_from_any_date(capsys, tmp_path):
    # Regression: a hardcoded default window reported 0h opportunity and a full
    # shortfall for any scenario that did not fall on the fixture's dates.
    code = main(

            str(shift_to_next_year("late-return-baseline.json", tmp_path)),

def test_explicit_window_still_narrows_the_report(capsys):

            str(FIXTURES / "late-return-candidate.json"),

            "2026-09-13T12:00",
            "America/Chicago",

    code = main([str(FIXTURES / "does-not-exist.json"), str(FIXTURES / "late-return-candidate.json")])
    assert code == 2
    assert "does-not-exist" in capsys.readouterr().err

    delta = fixture_comparison()
    text = render_comparison(delta).lower()
    if delta.baseline.conflicts:
        assert "conflict" in text

I've drafted a plan for a new `weekend.py` that builds scenarios from kickoff-band templates per night, reuses `evaluate()`/`compare()`, and flags fixed events that changed—getting this approach reviewed before writing tests.

The review confirmed the approach and clarified four details: curfew/wake-up are markers not events, `pre_bed_minutes` remains the sole wind-down field, nightly intervals are fixed by date rather than the proposed window, and changed-event detection must account for end times without splitting a kickoff move into multiple events. I'll start step 1 (kickoff anchoring) with failing tests while updating the task tracker for visibility.

"""Game-weekend model from SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md, Release 1 (Package 1b).

Every offset, curfew, and wake time here is synthetic. Round numbers are used on
purpose so nobody mistakes them for Baylor's real game-week timeline.
"""

from datetime import timedelta

from sleep_scheduler.schedule import KickoffAnchor
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime

CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
DENVER = "America/Denver"

H = timedelta(hours=1)


# --- Kickoff anchoring -------------------------------------------------------


def test_kickoff_relative_event_is_offset_in_elapsed_time_across_zones():
    # A Denver kickoff at 13:00 MT is 14:00 CT. Practice at kickoff - 24h, held
    # at home, must be 14:00 Friday in Chicago: elapsed hours from the kickoff
    # instant, not the Denver wall clock copied into Chicago.
    kickoff = LocalTime("2026-10-03T13:00", DENVER).instant
    practice = KickoffAnchor(start=-24 * H, end=-22 * H, start_zone=CHICAGO).resolve(kickoff)
    assert practice.start == kickoff - 24 * H
    assert practice.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T14:00"
    assert practice.wall("end") == "2026-10-02T16:00"


def test_travel_leg_anchor_keeps_departure_and_arrival_zones():
    kickoff = LocalTime("2026-10-03T13:00", DENVER).instant
    flight = KickoffAnchor(
        start=-20 * H, end=-18 * H, start_zone=CHICAGO, end_zone=DENVER
    ).resolve(kickoff)
    assert (flight.start_zone, flight.end_zone) == (CHICAGO, DENVER)
    assert flight.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T18:00"
    assert flight.wall("end") == "2026-10-02T19:00"


def test_changing_kickoff_moves_an_anchored_event_by_the_same_elapsed_amount():
    anchor = KickoffAnchor(start=-4 * H, end=-3 * H, start_zone=DENVER)
    early = anchor.resolve(LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:00", DENVER).instant)
    late = anchor.resolve(LocalTime("2026-10-03T14:30", DENVER).instant)
    assert late.start - early.start == timedelta(hours=3, minutes=30)
    assert late.duration == early.duration == H

entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1's late-return comparison actually uses. The
spec's AthleteProfile, group membership, and scenario revisions are deliberately
absent: they depend on the unanswered question of whether the modelling unit is
a representative athlete, a subgroup, or an individual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin; ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed before an obligation
    starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is inferred.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None

    @property
    def mandatory(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind not in OPTIONAL_KINDS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    It is never inferred from free time. ``kind`` records where the opportunity
    sits (hotel, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

    id: str
    label: str
    interval: Interval
    kind: str = "hotel"
    proposed: bool = False


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """A named plan: obligations, entered sleep windows, and its assumptions."""

    id: str
    title: str
    display_zone: str
    events: list[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
    windows: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = field(default_factory=list)
    assumptions: AssumptionSet | None = None

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.mandatory]

"""Game-weekend model from SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md, Release 1 (Package 1b).

Every offset, curfew, and wake time here is synthetic. Round numbers are used on
purpose so nobody mistakes them for Baylor's real game-week timeline.
"""

from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.schedule import KickoffAnchor
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import band_for

CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
DENVER = "America/Denver"

H = timedelta(hours=1)


# --- Kickoff anchoring -------------------------------------------------------


def test_kickoff_relative_event_is_offset_in_elapsed_time_across_zones():
    # A Denver kickoff at 13:00 MT is 14:00 CT. Practice at kickoff - 24h, held
    # at home, must be 14:00 Friday in Chicago: elapsed hours from the kickoff
    # instant, not the Denver wall clock copied into Chicago.
    kickoff = LocalTime("2026-10-03T13:00", DENVER).instant
    practice = KickoffAnchor(start=-24 * H, end=-22 * H, start_zone=CHICAGO).resolve(kickoff)
    assert practice.start == kickoff - 24 * H
    assert practice.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T14:00"
    assert practice.wall("end") == "2026-10-02T16:00"


def test_travel_leg_anchor_keeps_departure_and_arrival_zones():
    kickoff = LocalTime("2026-10-03T13:00", DENVER).instant
    flight = KickoffAnchor(
        start=-20 * H, end=-18 * H, start_zone=CHICAGO, end_zone=DENVER
    ).resolve(kickoff)
    assert (flight.start_zone, flight.end_zone) == (CHICAGO, DENVER)
    assert flight.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T18:00"
    assert flight.wall("end") == "2026-10-02T19:00"


def test_changing_kickoff_moves_an_anchored_event_by_the_same_elapsed_amount():
    anchor = KickoffAnchor(start=-4 * H, end=-3 * H, start_zone=DENVER)
    early = anchor.resolve(LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:00", DENVER).instant)
    late = anchor.resolve(LocalTime("2026-10-03T14:30", DENVER).instant)
    assert late.start - early.start == timedelta(hours=3, minutes=30)
    assert late.duration == early.duration == H


# --- Kickoff bands -----------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("wall", "band"),
    [
        ("2026-10-03T11:59", "early"),
        ("2026-10-03T12:00", "afternoon"),
        ("2026-10-03T17:59", "afternoon"),
        ("2026-10-03T18:00", "night"),
    ],
)
def test_band_boundaries_at_noon_and_six_pm(wall, band):
    assert band_for(LocalTime(wall, DENVER), game_zone=DENVER) == band


def test_band_is_judged_in_the_game_zone_not_the_zone_kickoff_was_entered_in():
    # Entered as noon Chicago time, but that is 11:00 at the Denver stadium.
    assert band_for(LocalTime("2026-10-03T12:00", CHICAGO), game_zone=DENVER) == "early"

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .temporal import LocalTime

__all__ = ["band_for"]


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"

from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import KickoffBandTemplate, NightMarker, TemplateEntry

CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
DENVER = "America/Denver"
H = timedelta(hours=1)

EARLY_KICKOFF = LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:00", DENVER)

    sleep_target_hours=8.0,
    pre_bed_minutes=30,
    morning_minutes=0,
    source="synthetic test assumptions",
)


def road_early_template() -> KickoffBandTemplate:
    return KickoffBandTemplate(
        band="early",
        game_type="road",
        source="synthetic test template",
        entries=(
            # Fri 15:00-17:00 CT
            TemplateEntry("fri-practice", "practice", "Friday practice", -21 * H, -19 * H, movable=True),
            # Fri 19:00 CT -> 20:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("fri-depart", "travel", "Charter to game city", -17 * H, -15 * H,
                          start_at="home", end_at="away", movable=True),
            # Fri 21:00-22:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("fri-meeting", "meeting", "Team meetings", -14 * H, -13 * H,
                          start_at="away", movable=True),
            # Sat 07:00-08:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("sat-meal", "meal", "Pregame meal", -4 * H, -3 * H, start_at="away"),
            # Sat 11:00-15:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("game", "game", "Game", 0 * H, 4 * H, start_at="away"),
            # Sat 17:00 MT -> 20:00 CT
            TemplateEntry("sat-depart", "travel", "Return charter", 6 * H, 8 * H,
                          start_at="away", end_at="home", movable=True),
        ),
        nights=(
            # Thu 23:00 CT to Fri 07:00 CT
            NightMarker("thu", curfew=-37 * H, wake=-29 * H, at="home"),
            # Fri 23:00 MT to Sat 06:00 MT
            NightMarker("fri", curfew=-12 * H, wake=-5 * H, at="away"),
            # Sat 23:00 CT; Sunday is an off day, so the wake is assumed
            NightMarker("sat", curfew=11 * H, wake=None, at="home"),
        ),
    )

"""Kickoff-band templates expanded into a game-weekend scenario."""

from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.schedule import Event, KickoffAnchor
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval, LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import build_weekend
from synthetic import ASSUMPTIONS, CHICAGO, DENVER, EARLY_KICKOFF, H, road_early_template


def build(kickoff=EARLY_KICKOFF, **kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        road_early_template(),
        kickoff,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=ASSUMPTIONS,
        id="baseline",
        title="Early road kickoff (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def events(weekend):
    return {e.id: e for e in weekend.scenario.events}


def test_template_entries_become_events_placed_from_kickoff():
    practice = events(build())["fri-practice"]
    # 11:00 MT Saturday is 12:00 CT; minus 21 elapsed hours is 15:00 CT Friday.
    assert practice.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T15:00"
    assert practice.anchor == KickoffAnchor(-21 * H, -19 * H, CHICAGO, CHICAGO)


def test_travel_entry_departs_home_and_arrives_in_the_game_zone():
    flight = events(build())["fri-depart"]
    assert (flight.interval.start_zone, flight.interval.end_zone) == (CHICAGO, DENVER)
    assert flight.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T19:00"
    assert flight.interval.wall("end") == "2026-10-02T20:00"


def test_same_template_at_a_later_kickoff_keeps_offsets_and_moves_instants():
    early = events(build())
    later = events(build(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER)))
    for event_id, event in early.items():
        assert later[event_id].anchor == event.anchor
        assert later[event_id].interval.start - event.interval.start == timedelta(minutes=30)


def test_absolute_events_do_not_move_when_kickoff_changes():
    film = Event(
        id="thu-film",
        kind="meeting",
        title="Thursday film",
        interval=Interval.of("2026-10-01T19:00", "2026-10-01T20:00", CHICAGO),
    )
    early = events(build(extra_events=[film]))
    later = events(build(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER), extra_events=[film]))
    assert later["thu-film"].interval == early["thu-film"].interval
    assert later["thu-film"].anchor is None


def test_movable_flags_come_from_the_template():
    evs = events(build())
    assert all(evs[i].movable for i in ("fri-practice", "fri-depart", "fri-meeting", "sat-depart"))
    assert not evs["game"].movable
    assert not evs["sat-meal"].movable


def test_curfew_and_wake_up_are_not_scheduled_as_obligations():
    # Event kinds are mandatory by default, so a curfew entered as an event
    # would block the very sleep window it is meant to bound.
    scenario_events = build().scenario.events
    assert len(scenario_events) == len(road_early_template().entries)
    assert not {e.kind for e in scenario_events} & {"curfew", "wake", "wake-up"}


def test_offset_override_moves_only_the_named_entry():
    base = events(build())
    moved = events(build(offsets={"fri-meeting": (-15 * H, -14 * H)}))
    assert moved["fri-meeting"].interval.start - base["fri-meeting"].interval.start == -H
    assert all(moved[i].interval == base[i].interval for i in base if i != "fri-meeting")


def test_override_naming_an_unknown_entry_is_refused():
    # A typo must not silently leave the schedule unchanged.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="fri-meetng"):
        build(offsets={"fri-meetng": (-15 * H, -14 * H)})


def test_template_for_the_wrong_band_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="band"):
        build(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T14:30", DENVER))


def test_scenario_carries_the_assumptions_and_home_display_zone():
    scenario = build().scenario
    assert scenario.assumptions == ASSUMPTIONS
    assert scenario.display_zone == CHICAGO

"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1's late-return comparison actually uses. The
spec's AthleteProfile, group membership, and scenario revisions are deliberately
absent: they depend on the unanswered question of whether the modelling unit is
a representative athlete, a subgroup, or an individual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "KickoffAnchor", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin; ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed before an obligation
    starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is inferred.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffAnchor:
    """An event placed by its offset from kickoff rather than by clock time.

    Offsets are elapsed time from the kickoff *instant*. Resolving through the
    instant, not the wall clock, is what keeps "kickoff - 24h" correct when the
    event happens at home and the game is played in another zone.
    """

    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_zone: str
    end_zone: str | None = None

    def resolve(self, kickoff: datetime) -> Interval:
        return Interval(
            kickoff + self.start,
            kickoff + self.end,
            start_zone=self.start_zone,
            end_zone=self.end_zone or self.start_zone,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None

    @property
    def mandatory(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind not in OPTIONAL_KINDS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    It is never inferred from free time. ``kind`` records where the opportunity
    sits (hotel, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

    id: str
    label: str
    interval: Interval
    kind: str = "hotel"
    proposed: bool = False


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """A named plan: obligations, entered sleep windows, and its assumptions."""

    id: str
    title: str
    display_zone: str
    events: list[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
    windows: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = field(default_factory=list)
    assumptions: AssumptionSet | None = None

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.mandatory]

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, Scenario
from .temporal import LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",

"""The protected sleep window rule, per night of a game weekend.

start = the later of curfew and (last obligation end + wind-down buffer)
end   = the wake-up call; Saturday night ends at an assumed wake time instead,
        because Sunday is a player off day and nothing else bounds it.

Synthetic weekend (see tests/synthetic.py): Friday curfew 23:00 MT, wake-up
06:00 MT, meetings 21:00-22:00 MT, 30-minute wind-down buffer.
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.opportunity import evaluate
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval, LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import WindowOverride, build_weekend
from synthetic import ASSUMPTIONS, CHICAGO, DENVER, EARLY_KICKOFF, H, road_early_template

WITH_WAKE = replace(ASSUMPTIONS, saturday_night_wake="09:00")
NO_WAKE = replace(ASSUMPTIONS, saturday_night_wake=None)
M = timedelta(minutes=1)


def build(assumptions=WITH_WAKE, **kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        road_early_template(),
        EARLY_KICKOFF,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=assumptions,
        id="baseline",
        title="Early road kickoff (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def night(weekend, name):
    return next(n for n in weekend.nights if n.night == name)


def test_friday_window_runs_from_curfew_to_wake_up_when_curfew_binds():
    window = night(build(), "fri").window
    assert window.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T23:00"
    assert window.interval.wall("end") == "2026-10-03T06:00"
    assert (window.start_source, window.end_source) == ("curfew", "wake-up call")


def test_away_night_is_a_hotel_window_and_home_nights_are_home_windows():
    weekend = build()
    assert [night(weekend, n).window.kind for n in ("thu", "fri", "sat")] == ["home", "hotel", "home"]


def test_moving_friday_meetings_earlier_leaves_the_window_unchanged_while_curfew_binds():
    base = night(build(), "fri").window.interval
    moved = night(build(offsets={"fri-meeting": (-16 * H, -15 * H)}), "fri").window.interval
    assert moved == base


def test_meetings_ending_after_curfew_minus_buffer_shorten_the_night_by_the_overrun():
    # Meetings now end 22:50 MT; plus 30 minutes is 23:20, 20 minutes past curfew.
    base = night(build(), "fri").window
    late = night(build(offsets={"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - 10 * M)}), "fri").window
    assert late.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T23:20"
    assert late.start_source == "obligation:fri-meeting"
    assert base.interval.duration - late.interval.duration == 20 * M


def test_the_wind_down_buffer_comes_from_the_assumption_set():
    late = night(
        build(
            assumptions=replace(WITH_WAKE, pre_bed_minutes=60),
            offsets={"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - 10 * M)},
        ),
        "fri",
    ).window
    assert late.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T23:50"


def test_saturday_night_ends_at_the_assumed_wake_time_labelled_as_an_assumption():
    window = night(build(), "sat").window
    assert window.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-03T23:00"
    assert window.interval.end_zone == CHICAGO
    assert window.interval.wall("end") == "2026-10-04T09:00"
    assert window.end_source == "assumed wake"


def test_late_return_shortens_saturday_night_against_the_assumed_wake():
    # Return charter 01:00 MT -> 04:00 CT Sunday; plus 30 minutes is 04:30.
    window = night(build(offsets={"sat-depart": (14 * H, 16 * H)}), "sat").window
    assert window.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-04T04:30"
    assert window.start_source == "obligation:sat-depart"
    assert window.interval.duration == timedelta(hours=4, minutes=30)


def test_saturday_night_without_an_assumed_wake_time_is_refused():
    # Missing is not zero: an unbounded or silently empty Saturday would
    # misreport what a late return costs.
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="wake"):
        build(assumptions=NO_WAKE)


def test_staff_override_of_a_window_edge_is_applied_and_recorded():
    window = night(
        build(window_overrides={"fri": WindowOverride(start=LocalTime("2026-10-02T22:30", DENVER))}),
        "fri",
    ).window
    assert window.interval.wall("start") == "2026-10-02T22:30"
    assert (window.start_source, window.end_source) == ("staff override", "wake-up call")


def test_override_for_an_unknown_night_is_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="friday"):
        build(window_overrides={"friday": WindowOverride(start=LocalTime("2026-10-02T22:30", DENVER))})


def test_proposed_windows_are_on_the_scenario_so_evaluate_counts_them():
    weekend = build()
    report = evaluate(weekend.scenario, Interval.of("2026-10-02T18:00", "2026-10-03T12:00", DENVER))
    assert report.hours == 7.0
    assert all(w.proposed for w in weekend.scenario.windows)


def test_obligation_running_past_wake_up_leaves_no_window_and_says_why():

"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1 actually uses. The spec's AthleteProfile, group
membership, and subgroups are deliberately absent: the confirmed design models
one group per scenario, the travel party on the road or the whole roster at home.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "KickoffAnchor", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin (the wind-down buffer); ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed
    before an obligation starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is
    inferred.

    ``saturday_night_wake`` is a wall time such as ``"09:00"``. Sunday is a
    player off day, so no obligation ends Saturday night; this assumed wake time
    does, and reports must label it as an assumption.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str
    saturday_night_wake: str | None = None

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffAnchor:
    """An event placed by its offset from kickoff rather than by clock time.

    Offsets are elapsed time from the kickoff *instant*. Resolving through the
    instant, not the wall clock, is what keeps "kickoff - 24h" correct when the
    event happens at home and the game is played in another zone.
    """

    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_zone: str
    end_zone: str | None = None

    def resolve(self, kickoff: datetime) -> Interval:
        return Interval(
            kickoff + self.start,
            kickoff + self.end,
            start_zone=self.start_zone,
            end_zone=self.end_zone or self.start_zone,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None
    # Set when the event was placed from kickoff. ``interval`` is still the
    # resolved truth; the anchor records how it was derived.
    anchor: KickoffAnchor | None = None

    @property
    def mandatory(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind not in OPTIONAL_KINDS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    It is never inferred from free time. ``kind`` records where the opportunity
    sits (hotel, home, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

    id: str
    label: str
    interval: Interval
    kind: str = "hotel"
    proposed: bool = False
    # For a rule-proposed window, what set each edge: "curfew",
    # "obligation:<event id>", "wake-up call", "assumed wake", "staff override".
    start_source: str | None = None
    end_source: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """A named plan: obligations, entered sleep windows, and its assumptions."""

    id: str
    title: str
    display_zone: str
    events: list[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
    windows: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = field(default_factory=list)
    assumptions: AssumptionSet | None = None

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.mandatory]

"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1's late-return comparison actually uses. The
spec's AthleteProfile, group membership, and scenario revisions are deliberately
absent: they depend on the unanswered question of whether the modelling unit is
a representative athlete, a subgroup, or an individual.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "KickoffAnchor", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin; ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed before an obligation
    starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is inferred.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffAnchor:
    """An event placed by its offset from kickoff rather than by clock time.

    Offsets are elapsed time from the kickoff *instant*. Resolving through the
    instant, not the wall clock, is what keeps "kickoff - 24h" correct when the
    event happens at home and the game is played in another zone.
    """

    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_zone: str
    end_zone: str | None = None

    def resolve(self, kickoff: datetime) -> Interval:
        return Interval(
            kickoff + self.start,
            kickoff + self.end,
            start_zone=self.start_zone,
            end_zone=self.end_zone or self.start_zone,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None

    # resolved truth; the anchor records how it was derived.

class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    sits (hotel, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

@dataclass
class Scenario:

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.

Each night then gets one rule-proposed protected sleep window:

* start = the later of curfew and (last obligation end + wind-down buffer)
* end   = the wake-up call, or for a night with none (Saturday, before the
  Sunday off day) the assumed wake time from the assumption set

Every edge records what set it, so the report can say "curfew" or "meetings
ran late" rather than presenting a bare number.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
from .temporal import Interval, LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",
    "NightMarker",
    "NightPlan",
    "TemplateEntry",
    "WindowOverride",
    "band_for",
    "build_weekend",
]


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEntry:
    """One obligation in a kickoff-band template, placed by offset from kickoff.

    ``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are ``"home"`` or ``"away"``; a travel leg has
    both. They become real IANA zones only when the template is applied to a
    specific game.
    """

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_at: str = "home"
    end_at: str | None = None
    movable: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightMarker:
    """Curfew and wake-up for one night, as offsets from kickoff.

    Deliberately not an Event: event kinds are mandatory by default, so a
    curfew scheduled as an obligation would block the sleep it bounds.
    ``wake=None`` means the night has no wake-up call (Saturday, before the
    Sunday off day) and its end comes from the assumption set instead.
    """

    night: str
    curfew: timedelta
    wake: timedelta | None
    at: str = "home"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffBandTemplate:
    band: str
    game_type: str
    entries: tuple[TemplateEntry, ...]
    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WindowOverride:
    """A staff-entered edge that replaces the rule's start, end, or both."""

    start: LocalTime | None = None
    end: LocalTime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightPlan:
    """One night's proposed window, or ``None`` with the reason there is none."""

    night: str
    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from."""

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str
    nights: tuple[NightPlan, ...] = ()


def _assumed_wake(curfew: datetime, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:
    if not assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "
            "saturday_night_wake; set an assumed wake time rather than leaving "
            "the night unbounded"
        )
    local = curfew.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone))
    # A curfew before noon is already past midnight, so the wake is that day.
    day = local.date() + timedelta(days=1 if local.hour >= 12 else 0)
    return LocalTime(f"{day.isoformat()}T{assumptions.saturday_night_wake}", zone).instant


def _plan_night(
    marker: NightMarker,
    kickoff: datetime,
    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    curfew = kickoff + marker.curfew
    if marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = kickoff + marker.wake, "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(curfew, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    start, start_source = curfew, "curfew"
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < end:
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    if override is not None:
        if override.start is not None:
            start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"
        if override.end is not None:
            end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"

    if start >= end:
        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
        )

    window = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window)


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] | None = None,
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff and propose each night's sleep window.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does. ``window_overrides`` replaces
    a rule-proposed edge, keyed by night.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    edges = dict(window_overrides or {})
    unknown_nights = sorted(set(edges) - {marker.night for marker in template.nights})
    if unknown_nights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"window override names no night in the template: {', '.join(unknown_nights)}"
        )

    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extra_events)

    obligations = [event for event in events if event.mandatory]
    nights = tuple(
        _plan_night(
            marker, instant, zones[marker.at], obligations, assumptions, edges.get(marker.night)
        )
        for marker in template.nights
    )

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        windows=[plan.window for plan in nights if plan.window is not None],
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
        nights=nights,
    )
