    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WindowOverride:
    """A staff-entered edge that replaces the rule's start, end, or both."""

    start: LocalTime | None = None
    end: LocalTime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightPlan:
    """One night's proposed window, or ``None`` with the reason there is none."""

    night: str
    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from."""

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str
    nights: tuple[NightPlan, ...] = ()


def _assumed_wake(curfew: datetime, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:
    if not assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "
            "saturday_night_wake; set an assumed wake time rather than leaving "
            "the night unbounded"
        )
    local = curfew.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone))
    # A curfew before noon is already past midnight, so the wake is that day.
    day = local.date() + timedelta(days=1 if local.hour >= 12 else 0)
    return LocalTime(f"{day.isoformat()}T{assumptions.saturday_night_wake}", zone).instant


def _plan_night(
    marker: NightMarker,
    kickoff: datetime,
    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    curfew = kickoff + marker.curfew
    if marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = kickoff + marker.wake, "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(curfew, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    start, start_source = curfew, "curfew"
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < end:
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    if override is not None:
        if override.start is not None:
            start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"
        if override.end is not None:
            end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"

    if start >= end:
        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
        )

    window = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window)


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] | None = None,
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff and propose each night's sleep window.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does. ``window_overrides`` replaces
    a rule-proposed edge, keyed by night.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    edges = dict(window_overrides or {})
    unknown_nights = sorted(set(edges) - {marker.night for marker in template.nights})
    if unknown_nights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"window override names no night in the template: {', '.join(unknown_nights)}"
        )

    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extra_events)

    obligations = [event for event in events if event.mandatory]
    nights = tuple(
        _plan_night(
            marker, instant, zones[marker.at], obligations, assumptions, edges.get(marker.night)
        )
        for marker in template.nights
    )

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        windows=[plan.window for plan in nights if plan.window is not None],
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
        nights=nights,
    )

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, Scenario
from .temporal import LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",
    "NightMarker",
    "TemplateEntry",
    "band_for",
    "build_weekend",
]


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEntry:
    """One obligation in a kickoff-band template, placed by offset from kickoff.

    ``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are ``"home"`` or ``"away"``; a travel leg has
    both. They become real IANA zones only when the template is applied to a
    specific game.
    """

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_at: str = "home"
    end_at: str | None = None
    movable: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightMarker:
    """Curfew and wake-up for one night, as offsets from kickoff.

    Deliberately not an Event: event kinds are mandatory by default, so a
    curfew scheduled as an obligation would block the sleep it bounds.
    ``wake=None`` means the night has no wake-up call (Saturday, before the
    Sunday off day) and its end comes from the assumption set instead.
    """

    night: str
    curfew: timedelta
    wake: timedelta | None
    at: str = "home"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffBandTemplate:
    band: str
    game_type: str
    entries: tuple[TemplateEntry, ...]
    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from."""

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extra_events)

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
    )

"""Synthetic game-weekend inputs shared by the weekend tests.

Offsets are round hours chosen to be obviously invented. They are not Baylor's
game-week timeline; staff will supply the real values per kickoff band.

The weekend: an early road kickoff at 11:00 Mountain on Saturday 2026-10-03,
home in Central time. Wall times below are what each offset resolves to.
"""

from datetime import timedelta

from sleep_scheduler.schedule import AssumptionSet
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import KickoffBandTemplate, NightMarker, TemplateEntry

CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
DENVER = "America/Denver"
H = timedelta(hours=1)

EARLY_KICKOFF = LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:00", DENVER)

ASSUMPTIONS = AssumptionSet(
    sleep_target_hours=8.0,
    pre_bed_minutes=30,
    morning_minutes=0,
    source="synthetic test assumptions",
)


def road_early_template() -> KickoffBandTemplate:
    return KickoffBandTemplate(
        band="early",
        game_type="road",
        source="synthetic test template",
        entries=(
            # Fri 15:00-17:00 CT
            TemplateEntry("fri-practice", "practice", "Friday practice", -21 * H, -19 * H, movable=True),
            # Fri 19:00 CT -> 20:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("fri-depart", "travel", "Charter to game city", -17 * H, -15 * H,
                          start_at="home", end_at="away", movable=True),
            # Fri 21:00-22:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("fri-meeting", "meeting", "Team meetings", -14 * H, -13 * H,
                          start_at="away", movable=True),
            # Sat 07:00-08:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("sat-meal", "meal", "Pregame meal", -4 * H, -3 * H, start_at="away"),
            # Sat 11:00-15:00 MT
            TemplateEntry("game", "game", "Game", 0 * H, 4 * H, start_at="away"),
            # Sat 17:00 MT -> 20:00 CT
            TemplateEntry("sat-depart", "travel", "Return charter", 6 * H, 8 * H,
                          start_at="away", end_at="home", movable=True),
        ),
        nights=(
            # Thu 23:00 CT to Fri 07:00 CT
            NightMarker("thu", curfew=-37 * H, wake=-29 * H, at="home"),
            # Fri 23:00 MT to Sat 06:00 MT
            NightMarker("fri", curfew=-12 * H, wake=-5 * H, at="away"),
            # Sat 23:00 CT; Sunday is an off day, so the wake is assumed
            NightMarker("sat", curfew=11 * H, wake=None, at="home"),
        ),
    )

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.

Each night then gets one rule-proposed protected sleep window:

* start = the later of curfew and (last obligation end + wind-down buffer)
* end   = the wake-up call, or for a night with none (Saturday, before the
  Sunday off day) the assumed wake time from the assumption set

Every edge records what set it, so the report can say "curfew" or "meetings
ran late" rather than presenting a bare number.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .opportunity import Comparison, EventChange, OpportunityReport, compare, evaluate, event_changes
from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
from .temporal import Interval, LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",
    "NightMarker",
    "NightPlan",
    "NightReport",
    "TemplateEntry",
    "WeekendComparison",
    "WeekendReport",
    "WindowOverride",
    "band_for",
    "build_weekend",
    "compare_weekends",
    "evaluate_weekend",
]

# Each night is reported over the same clock span, fixed by date. Deriving it
# from the proposed window would give a candidate whose meetings ran late a
# different interval from its baseline, and the comparison would refuse them.
NIGHT_REPORT_START = "18:00"
NIGHT_REPORT_END = "12:00"


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEntry:
    """One obligation in a kickoff-band template, placed by offset from kickoff.

    ``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are ``"home"`` or ``"away"``; a travel leg has
    both. They become real IANA zones only when the template is applied to a
    specific game.
    """

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_at: str = "home"
    end_at: str | None = None
    movable: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightMarker:
    """Curfew and wake-up for one night, as offsets from kickoff.

    Deliberately not an Event: event kinds are mandatory by default, so a
    curfew scheduled as an obligation would block the sleep it bounds.
    ``wake=None`` means the night has no wake-up call (Saturday, before the
    Sunday off day) and its end comes from the assumption set instead.
    """

    night: str
    curfew: timedelta
    wake: timedelta | None
    at: str = "home"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffBandTemplate:
    band: str
    game_type: str
    entries: tuple[TemplateEntry, ...]
    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WindowOverride:
    """A staff-entered edge that replaces the rule's start, end, or both."""

    start: LocalTime | None = None
    end: LocalTime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightPlan:
    """One night's proposed window, or ``None`` with the reason there is none."""

    night: str
    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""
    reporting: Interval | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from."""

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str
    nights: tuple[NightPlan, ...] = ()


def _night_date(curfew: datetime, zone: str) -> date:
    local = curfew.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone))
    # A curfew before noon is already past midnight: it belongs to the night
    # that started the previous evening.

    # that started the previous evening.
    return local.date() if local.hour >= 12 else local.date() - timedelta(days=1)


def _assumed_wake(night_date: date, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:
    if not assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "
            "saturday_night_wake; set an assumed wake time rather than leaving "
            "the night unbounded"
        )
    morning = night_date + timedelta(days=1)
    return LocalTime(f"{morning.isoformat()}T{assumptions.saturday_night_wake}", zone).instant


def _plan_night(
    marker: NightMarker,
    kickoff: datetime,
    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    curfew = kickoff + marker.curfew
    night_date = _night_date(curfew, zone)
    reporting = Interval.of(
        f"{night_date.isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_START}",
        f"{(night_date + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_END}",
        zone,
    )

    if marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = kickoff + marker.wake, "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(night_date, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    start, start_source = curfew, "curfew"
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < end:
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    if override is not None:
        if override.start is not None:
            start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"
        if override.end is not None:
            end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"

    if start >= end:
        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
            reporting=reporting,
        )

    window = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window, reporting=reporting)


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] | None = None,
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff and propose each night's sleep window.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does. ``window_overrides`` replaces
    a rule-proposed edge, keyed by night.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    edges = dict(window_overrides or {})
    unknown_nights = sorted(set(edges) - {marker.night for marker in template.nights})
    if unknown_nights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"window override names no night in the template: {', '.join(unknown_nights)}"
        )

    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extra_events)

    obligations = [event for event in events if event.mandatory]
    nights = tuple(
        _plan_night(
            marker, instant, zones[marker.at], obligations, assumptions, edges.get(marker.night)
        )
        for marker in template.nights
    )

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        windows=[plan.window for plan in nights if plan.window is not None],
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
        nights=nights,
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightReport:
    night: str
    plan: NightPlan
    report: OpportunityReport

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return self.report.hours

    @property
    def note(self) -> str:
        return self.plan.note


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WeekendReport:
    weekend: GameWeekend
    nights: tuple[NightReport, ...]

    def night(self, name: str) -> NightReport:
        for report in self.nights:
            if report.night == name:
                return report
        raise KeyError(f"no {name!r} night in this weekend")


def evaluate_weekend(weekend: GameWeekend) -> WeekendReport:
    """Opportunity for each night, over that night's date-fixed interval."""
    return WeekendReport(
        weekend=weekend,
        nights=tuple(
            NightReport(plan.night, plan, evaluate(weekend.scenario, plan.reporting))
            for plan in weekend.nights
        ),
    )


def _signed(delta: timedelta) -> str:
    minutes = round(delta.total_seconds() / 60)
    sign = "+" if minutes >= 0 else "-"
    minutes = abs(minutes)
    return f"{sign}{minutes // 60}h{minutes % 60:02d}m"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WeekendComparison:
    baseline: WeekendReport
    candidate: WeekendReport
    nights: tuple[tuple[str, Comparison], ...]
    changed_events: list[EventChange]
    kickoff_shift: timedelta

    def night(self, name: str) -> Comparison:
        for night, comparison in self.nights:
            if night == name:
                return comparison
        raise KeyError(f"no {name!r} night in this comparison")

    @property
    def fixed_event_changes(self) -> list[EventChange]:
        return [c for c in self.changed_events if not c.movable]

    @property
    def flags(self) -> list[str]:
        """Plain-language warnings that the candidate moved something fixed.

        Flagged rather than refused: staff may legitimately explore a
        different kickoff, but nobody should win an argument by doing it
        quietly.
        """
        flags = []
        if self.kickoff_shift:
            flags.append(f"kickoff moved {_signed(self.kickoff_shift)}; kickoff is fixed, not a lever")
        for change in self.fixed_event_changes:
            flags.append(
                f"{change.event_id} changed (start {_signed(change.shift)}, "
                f"end {_signed(change.end_shift)}) but is not a movable event"
            )
        return flags


def compare_weekends(baseline: GameWeekend, candidate: GameWeekend) -> WeekendComparison:
    """Night-by-night difference, plus what moved and whether it was allowed to."""
    before = evaluate_weekend(baseline)
    after = evaluate_weekend(candidate)
    names = [n.night for n in before.nights]
    if names != [n.night for n in after.nights]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"cannot compare weekends with different nights: {names} vs "
            f"{[n.night for n in after.nights]}"
        )
    return WeekendComparison(
        baseline=before,
        candidate=after,
        nights=tuple(
            (b.night, compare(b.report, a.report)) for b, a in zip(before.nights, after.nights)
        ),
        changed_events=event_changes(baseline.scenario, candidate.scenario),
        kickoff_shift=candidate.kickoff - baseline.kickoff,
    )

"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.

Each night then gets one rule-proposed protected sleep window:

* start = the later of curfew and (last obligation end + wind-down buffer)
* end   = the wake-up call, or for a night with none (Saturday, before the
  Sunday off day) the assumed wake time from the assumption set

Every edge records what set it, so the report can say "curfew" or "meetings
ran late" rather than presenting a bare number.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
from .temporal import Interval, LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",
    "NightMarker",
    "NightPlan",
    "TemplateEntry",
    "WindowOverride",
    "band_for",
    "build_weekend",
]


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEntry:
    """One obligation in a kickoff-band template, placed by offset from kickoff.

    ``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are ``"home"`` or ``"away"``; a travel leg has
    both. They become real IANA zones only when the template is applied to a
    specific game.
    """

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_at: str = "home"
    end_at: str | None = None
    movable: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightMarker:
    """Curfew and wake-up for one night, as offsets from kickoff.

    Deliberately not an Event: event kinds are mandatory by default, so a
    curfew scheduled as an obligation would block the sleep it bounds.
    ``wake=None`` means the night has no wake-up call (Saturday, before the
    Sunday off day) and its end comes from the assumption set instead.
    """

    night: str
    curfew: timedelta
    wake: timedelta | None
    at: str = "home"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffBandTemplate:
    band: str
    game_type: str
    entries: tuple[TemplateEntry, ...]
    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WindowOverride:
    """A staff-entered edge that replaces the rule's start, end, or both."""

    start: LocalTime | None = None
    end: LocalTime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightPlan:
    """One night's proposed window, or ``None`` with the reason there is none."""

    night: str
    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""

class GameWeekend:

    game_zone: str

def _assumed_wake(curfew: datetime, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:

            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "

            "the night unbounded"

    day = local.date() + timedelta(days=1 if local.hour >= 12 else 0)

    marker: NightMarker,

    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,

        if override.start is not None:
            start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"
        if override.end is not None:
            end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"

        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
        )

        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window)


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] | None = None,
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff and propose each night's sleep window.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does. ``window_overrides`` replaces
    a rule-proposed edge, keyed by night.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    edges = dict(window_overrides or {})
    unknown_nights = sorted(set(edges) - {marker.night for marker in template.nights})
    if unknown_nights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"window override names no night in the template: {', '.join(unknown_nights)}"
        )

    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extra_events)

    obligations = [event for event in events if event.mandatory]
    nights = tuple(
        _plan_night(
            marker, instant, zones[marker.at], obligations, assumptions, edges.get(marker.night)
        )
        for marker in template.nights
    )

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        windows=[plan.window for plan in nights if plan.window is not None],
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
        nights=nights,
    )

# Sleep Scheduler

A planned rebuild of the legacy FAST scheduling workflow for athlete sleep and team travel. The repository name is institution-neutral; the initial use case remains Baylor athletes and team travel.

## Current status

Research and static installer inspection are complete. A first slice of the application now exists: schedule modelling, sleep-opportunity calculation, scenario comparison, JSON persistence, and a command-line comparison over synthetic fixtures. **No forecasting engine has been selected, implemented, or validated**, and the four product questions recorded in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) remain unanswered. See [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) for what is built and what is deferred.

```bash
python -m pytest
PYTHONPATH=src python -m sleep_scheduler \
  fixtures/late-return-baseline.json fixtures/late-return-candidate.json
```

The tool reports sleep *opportunity* only. It has no vocabulary for effectiveness, fatigue, or readiness, and the sole model adapter returns a status rather than a number.

Start with:

- [Agent context and checkpoint](AGENTS.md)
- [Research report](FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md)
- [Proposed specification](SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md)
- [Installer inspection findings](installer-inspection/FINDINGS.md)

The specification contains proposals, not approved product decisions. Repository creation does not authorize implementation or resolve the paused interview.

## Archive boundary

This private repository tracks authored project documentation, inspection scripts, and future application code, tests, and synthetic fixtures. Original installers, proprietary binaries, bundled manuals/schema, screenshots, and staff/team schedules remain outside Git.

On the original Windows workstation the archive is located at:

```text
G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\99_UNSORTED\From_Desktop\TECHNOLOGY\FAST
```

Historical documents contain relative links into that archive. Links to `payload/`, `help/`, inventories, or original materials require local archive access; those assets are intentionally absent from a clone. Missing archive links do not mean extraction failed.

The active development checkout is outside OneDrive:

```text
C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\sleep-scheduler
```

## Inspection script

`installer-inspection/map-payload.ps1` maps already-extracted cabinet members to their original filenames and verifies sizes/hashes against the MSI. It does not install FAST or extract the cabinet. Supply `-ArchiveRoot` pointing to the archive above; its `installer-inspection/cab-raw/` must already exist. Generated payload and inventories are ignored by Git. The script refuses to overwrite an existing output payload.

## Development direction

Resolve the pending product interview, prototype one complete scheduling comparison, then finalize the specification and implementation tasks. Keep sleep opportunity distinct from actual sleep and preserve explicit model provenance for any future forecasts.

1	"""The forecasting seam, and the only adapter that currently exists.
2	
3	No engine has been selected or evaluated for this project. Rather than leave a
4	gap where someone later drops in a plausible-looking curve, the default adapter
5	is a placeholder that returns a *status*. Two spec rules are enforced here in
6	code rather than in prose:
7	
8	* An unsupported output is unavailable, never zero.
9	* Nothing emits a fatigue or effectiveness number under the FAST name without
10	  an adapter that has declared, and had recorded, its own evidence.
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	from dataclasses import dataclass
16	from datetime import datetime, timezone
17	from typing import Protocol
18	
19	from .opportunity import OpportunityReport
20	
21	__all__ = ["Capabilities", "ModelAdapter", "ModelResult", "UnevaluatedAdapter", "get_adapter"]
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class Capabilities:
26	    """What an adapter claims it can do. Claims still require evidence."""
27	
28	    outputs: tuple[str, ...]
29	    supports_travel: bool
30	    requires_sleep_history: bool
31	    evidence: str
32	
33	
34	@dataclass(frozen=True)
35	class ModelResult:
36	    """A forecast, or a documented reason there isn't one."""
37	
38	    adapter_name: str
39	    adapter_version: str
40	    available: bool
41	    reason: str
42	    generated_at: datetime
43	    series: dict[str, list[float]] | None = None
44	    summaries: dict[str, float] | None = None
45	
46	    def summary(self, name: str) -> float | None:
47	        """A requested summary, or ``None`` when unsupported. Never ``0.0``."""
48	        if not self.available or self.summaries is None:
49	            return None
50	        return self.summaries.get(name)
51	
52	
53	class ModelAdapter(Protocol):
54	    name: str
55	    version: str
56	
57	    def capabilities(self) -> Capabilities: ...
58	    def validate(self, report: OpportunityReport) -> list[str]: ...
59	    def simulate(self, report: OpportunityReport, *, requires_travel: bool = False) -> ModelResult: ...
60	
61	
62	class UnevaluatedAdapter:
63	    """The default: reports that no engine has been selected or evaluated."""
64	
65	    name = "unevaluated"
66	    version = "0.1.0"
67	
68	    def capabilities(self) -> Capabilities:
69	        return Capabilities(
70	            outputs=(),
71	            supports_travel=False,
72	            requires_sleep_history=False,
73	            evidence=(
74	                "None. No engine selected; SAFTE-FAST licensing and SAFTEr suitability "
75	                "both remain open questions in FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md."
76	            ),
77	        )
78	
79	    def validate(self, report: OpportunityReport) -> list[str]:
80	        warnings = [
81	            "A forecasting engine has not been evaluated for this population; "
82	            "opportunity figures carry no fatigue or effectiveness interpretation.",
83	        ]
84	        if report.conflicts:
85	            warnings.append(
86	                f"{len(report.conflicts)} scheduling conflict(s) remain unresolved in this scenario."
87	            )
88	        return warnings
89	
90	    def simulate(
91	        self, report: OpportunityReport, *, requires_travel: bool = False
92	    ) -> ModelResult:
93	        reason = (
94	            "Unavailable: no forecasting engine has been selected or evaluated for "
95	            "this project, so no effectiveness or fatigue value can be produced."
96	        )
97	        if requires_travel:
98	            reason += (
99	                " This scenario also requires transmeridian travel support, which "
100	                "this adapter does not provide."
101	            )
102	        return ModelResult(
103	            adapter_name=self.name,
104	            adapter_version=self.version,
105	            available=False,
106	            reason=reason,
107	            generated_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc),
108	        )
109	
110	
111	_ADAPTERS: dict[str, type] = {"unevaluated": UnevaluatedAdapter}
112	
113	
114	def get_adapter(name: str = "unevaluated") -> ModelAdapter:
115	    """Look up an adapter. Unknown names fail loudly rather than degrade."""
116	    try:
117	        return _ADAPTERS[name]()
118	    except KeyError:
119	        raise KeyError(
120	            f"no adapter registered as {name!r}; available: {sorted(_ADAPTERS)}"
121	        ) from None
122

"""Per-night reporting and comparison of two game weekends.

The decision this answers: does moving Friday practice, meetings, or a
departure change sleep opportunity on any night, and did the candidate quietly
move something that is not a lever?
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import build_weekend, compare_weekends, evaluate_weekend
from synthetic import ASSUMPTIONS, CHICAGO, DENVER, EARLY_KICKOFF, H, road_early_template

M = timedelta(minutes=1)
MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW = {"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - 10 * M)}  # 22:00-22:50 MT


def build(kickoff=EARLY_KICKOFF, id="baseline", assumptions=ASSUMPTIONS, **kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        road_early_template(),
        kickoff,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=assumptions,
        id=id,
        title=f"{id} (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def candidate(**kwargs):
    return build(id="candidate", **kwargs)


def test_each_night_of_the_weekend_is_reported_separately():
    report = evaluate_weekend(build())
    assert [n.night for n in report.nights] == ["thu", "fri", "sat"]
    # Thu 23:00-07:00 CT, Fri 23:00-06:00 MT, Sat 23:00 CT to assumed 09:00 CT.
    assert [n.hours for n in report.nights] == [8.0, 7.0, 10.0]


def test_night_reporting_interval_is_fixed_by_date_not_by_the_proposed_window():
    base = evaluate_weekend(build()).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    late = evaluate_weekend(candidate(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW)).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    assert late == base
    assert (base.wall("start"), base.wall("end")) == ("2026-10-02T18:00", "2026-10-03T12:00")
    assert base.start_zone == DENVER


def test_meetings_running_past_curfew_compare_cleanly_and_show_the_loss():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW))
    assert comparison.night("fri").hours_delta == pytest.approx(-20 / 60, abs=1e-6)
    assert comparison.night("thu").hours_delta == 0.0
    assert comparison.night("sat").hours_delta == 0.0


def test_moving_friday_practice_earlier_changes_no_night_while_curfew_binds():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"fri-practice": (-23 * H, -21 * H)}))
    assert [comparison.night(n).hours_delta for n in ("thu", "fri", "sat")] == [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.changed_events] == ["fri-practice"]
    assert comparison.fixed_event_changes == []
    assert comparison.flags == []


def test_kickoff_change_is_reported_once_not_as_every_anchored_event_moving():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER)))
    assert comparison.kickoff_shift == 30 * M
    assert comparison.changed_events == []


def test_kickoff_change_is_flagged_because_kickoff_is_not_a_lever():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER)))
    assert any("kickoff" in flag for flag in comparison.flags)


def test_candidate_that_moves_a_fixed_template_event_is_flagged():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"sat-meal": (-5 * H, -4 * H)}))
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.fixed_event_changes] == ["sat-meal"]
    assert any("sat-meal" in flag for flag in comparison.flags)


def test_late_return_costs_saturday_night_against_the_assumed_wake():
    # Return charter lands 04:00 CT instead of 20:00 CT: 10h becomes 4h30m.
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"sat-depart": (14 * H, 16 * H)}))
    assert comparison.night("sat").hours_delta == -5.5
    assert comparison.flags == []


def test_weekends_built_on_different_assumptions_are_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="assumption"):
        compare_weekends(build(), candidate(assumptions=replace(ASSUMPTIONS, pre_bed_minutes=60)))


def test_night_without_a_window_reports_zero_with_its_reason():
    night = evaluate_weekend(build(offsets={"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -4 * H - 30 * M)})).night("fri")
    assert night.hours == 0.0
    assert "fri-meeting" in night.note

"""JSON round-trip from SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md Package 3.

Completion criterion quoted from the spec: 'No event or zone changes on
round-trip'. The midnight-crossing case is the acceptance row that catches a
serializer that has quietly normalised everything to one zone.
"""

import json
from datetime import timedelta

from sleep_scheduler.opportunity import evaluate
from sleep_scheduler.persistence import scenario_from_dict, scenario_to_dict
from sleep_scheduler.schedule import (
    AssumptionSet,
    Event,
    KickoffAnchor,
    ProtectedSleepWindow,
    Scenario,
)
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval, LocalTime

CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
DENVER = "America/Denver"
OVERNIGHT = Interval.of("2026-09-12T18:00", "2026-09-13T12:00", CHICAGO)


def midnight_crossing_plan():
    return Scenario(
        id="late-return",
        title="Midnight crossing",
        display_zone=CHICAGO,
        events=[
            Event(
                "flight",
                "travel",
                "Return flight",
                Interval.of("2026-09-12T21:30", "2026-09-12T23:40", "America/Denver", CHICAGO),
            ),
            Event(
                "lift",
                "training",
                "Morning lift",
                Interval.of("2026-09-13T07:00", "2026-09-13T08:30", CHICAGO),
                movable=True,
            ),
        ],
        windows=[
            ProtectedSleepWindow(
                "hotel", "Overnight", Interval.of("2026-09-13T00:10", "2026-09-13T07:00", CHICAGO)
            )
        ],
        assumptions=AssumptionSet(8.0, 30, 45, "staff default"),
    )


def round_trip(plan):
    return scenario_from_dict(json.loads(json.dumps(scenario_to_dict(plan))))


def test_round_trip_preserves_every_event_instant_across_midnight():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert [e.interval for e in restored.events] == [e.interval for e in plan.events]


def test_round_trip_preserves_the_zone_each_time_was_entered_in():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    flight = restored.events[0]
    assert flight.interval.start.astimezone().tzinfo is not None
    assert scenario_to_dict(restored)["events"][0] == scenario_to_dict(plan)["events"][0]


def test_round_trip_leaves_opportunity_unchanged():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert evaluate(restored, OVERNIGHT).hours == evaluate(plan, OVERNIGHT).hours


def test_round_trip_preserves_assumptions_including_their_source():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert restored.assumptions == plan.assumptions


def test_round_trip_preserves_the_movable_flag_that_candidates_depend_on():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert [e.movable for e in restored.events] == [False, True]


def test_round_trip_preserves_window_kind_so_a_nap_stays_a_nap():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    plan.windows.append(
        ProtectedSleepWindow(
            "nap", "Afternoon", Interval.of("2026-09-13T14:00", "2026-09-13T15:00", CHICAGO), kind="nap"
        )
    )
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert [w.kind for w in restored.windows] == ["hotel", "nap"]


def test_serialized_scenario_carries_no_athlete_identifiers():
    blob = json.dumps(scenario_to_dict(midnight_crossing_plan()))
    assert "athlete" not in blob.lower()


# --- Fields added by the game-weekend model ----------------------------------
# Regression: the serializer builds dicts field by field, so these were
# silently dropped while the dict-comparison tests above kept passing.


def test_round_trip_preserves_a_kickoff_anchor():
    anchor = KickoffAnchor(-14 * timedelta(hours=1), -13 * timedelta(hours=1), DENVER, DENVER)
    kickoff = LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:00", DENVER).instant
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    plan.events.append(
        Event("fri-meeting", "meeting", "Team meetings", anchor.resolve(kickoff), movable=True, anchor=anchor)
    )
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    assert [e.anchor for e in restored.events] == [None, None, anchor]


def test_round_trip_preserves_where_each_window_edge_came_from():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    plan.windows[0] = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        "fri-night",
        "Fri night",
        Interval.of("2026-10-02T23:20", "2026-10-03T06:00", DENVER),
        proposed=True,
        start_source="obligation:fri-meeting",
        end_source="wake-up call",
    )
    restored = round_trip(plan)
    window = restored.windows[0]
    assert (window.start_source, window.end_source) == ("obligation:fri-meeting", "wake-up call")


def test_round_trip_preserves_the_saturday_night_assumed_wake():
    plan = midnight_crossing_plan()
    plan.assumptions = AssumptionSet(8.0, 30, 0, "staff default", saturday_night_wake="09:00")
    assert round_trip(plan).assumptions.saturday_night_wake == "09:00"


def test_a_scenario_saved_before_these_fields_existed_still_loads():
    payload = scenario_to_dict(midnight_crossing_plan())
    for event in payload["events"]:
        event.pop("anchor", None)
    for window in payload["windows"]:
        window.pop("start_source", None)
        window.pop("end_source", None)
    payload["assumptions"].pop("saturday_night_wake", None)
    restored = scenario_from_dict(payload)
    assert restored.assumptions.saturday_night_wake is None
    assert all(e.anchor is None for e in restored.events)

"""Game-weekend files: what staff enter, rebuilt through build_weekend on load.

The file stores inputs (template, kickoff, zones, assumptions, overrides), not
resolved instants. Rebuilding on load is what keeps kickoff anchoring in one
place: change the kickoff in the file and every anchored event moves with it.
"""

import json

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.persistence import (
    load_weekend,
    save_weekend,
    scenario_to_dict,
    weekend_from_dict,
    weekend_to_dict,
)
from sleep_scheduler.schedule import Event
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval, LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import WindowOverride, build_weekend
from synthetic import ASSUMPTIONS, CHICAGO, DENVER, EARLY_KICKOFF, H, road_early_template

MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW = {"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - H / 6)}  # 22:00-22:50 MT


def build(**kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        road_early_template(),
        EARLY_KICKOFF,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=ASSUMPTIONS,
        id="baseline",
        title="Early road kickoff (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def round_trip(weekend):
    return weekend_from_dict(json.loads(json.dumps(weekend_to_dict(weekend))))


def test_round_trip_rebuilds_the_same_events_and_windows():
    weekend = build()
    assert scenario_to_dict(round_trip(weekend).scenario) == scenario_to_dict(weekend.scenario)


def test_round_trip_keeps_the_template_kickoff_and_zones():
    weekend = build()
    restored = round_trip(weekend)
    assert restored.template == weekend.template
    assert restored.kickoff == weekend.kickoff
    assert (restored.home_zone, restored.game_zone) == (CHICAGO, DENVER)


def test_offset_overrides_are_stored_in_minutes_and_survive_the_round_trip():
    weekend = build(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW)
    payload = weekend_to_dict(weekend)
    assert payload["offsets"] == {"fri-meeting": {"start_minutes": -780, "end_minutes": -730}}
    assert scenario_to_dict(round_trip(weekend).scenario) == scenario_to_dict(weekend.scenario)


def test_window_overrides_and_extra_events_survive_the_round_trip():
    film = Event(
        id="thu-film",
        kind="meeting",
        title="Thursday film",
        interval=Interval.of("2026-10-01T19:00", "2026-10-01T20:00", CHICAGO),
    )
    weekend = build(
        extra_events=[film],
        window_overrides={"fri": WindowOverride(start=LocalTime("2026-10-02T22:30", DENVER))},
    )
    restored = round_trip(weekend)
    assert scenario_to_dict(restored.scenario) == scenario_to_dict(weekend.scenario)
    assert restored.scenario.windows[1].start_source == "staff override"


def test_editing_kickoff_in_the_file_moves_every_anchored_event():
    payload = weekend_to_dict(build())
    payload["kickoff"]["wall"] = "2026-10-03T11:30"
    moved = weekend_from_dict(payload)
    original = {e.id: e for e in build().scenario.events}
    for event in moved.scenario.events:
        assert event.interval.start - original[event.id].interval.start == H / 2


def test_a_plain_scenario_file_is_not_accepted_as_a_weekend():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="game-weekend"):
        weekend_from_dict(scenario_to_dict(build().scenario))


def test_save_and_load_a_weekend_file(tmp_path):
    weekend = build(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW)
    path = tmp_path / "candidate.json"
    save_weekend(weekend, path)
    assert scenario_to_dict(load_weekend(path).scenario) == scenario_to_dict(weekend.scenario)

input.content:
"""The game-weekend model: kickoff bands, templates, and the sleep window rule.

A Release 1 scenario is one football game weekend, Thursday evening through
Sunday midday. Its game-related events are placed by offset from kickoff, taken
from the template for the kickoff's band, so a TV-driven kickoff change re-flows
the whole weekend without retyping it.

Each night then gets one rule-proposed protected sleep window:

* start = the later of curfew and (last obligation end + wind-down buffer)
* end   = the wake-up call, or for a night with none (Saturday, before the
  Sunday off day) the assumed wake time from the assumption set

Every edge records what set it, so the report can say "curfew" or "meetings
ran late" rather than presenting a bare number.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Iterable, Mapping
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .opportunity import Comparison, EventChange, OpportunityReport, compare, evaluate, event_changes
from .schedule import AssumptionSet, Event, KickoffAnchor, ProtectedSleepWindow, Scenario
from .temporal import Interval, LocalTime

__all__ = [
    "GameWeekend",
    "KickoffBandTemplate",
    "NightMarker",
    "NightPlan",
    "NightReport",
    "TemplateEntry",
    "WeekendComparison",
    "WeekendReport",
    "WindowOverride",
    "band_for",
    "build_weekend",
    "compare_weekends",
    "evaluate_weekend",
]

# Each night is reported over the same clock span, fixed by date. Deriving it
# from the proposed window would give a candidate whose meetings ran late a
# different interval from its baseline, and the comparison would refuse them.
NIGHT_REPORT_START = "18:00"
NIGHT_REPORT_END = "12:00"


def band_for(kickoff: LocalTime, game_zone: str) -> str:
    """Which kickoff-band template applies: early, afternoon, or night.

    Judged on the stadium's clock. A kickoff entered in another zone is
    converted first, because noon in Waco is 11:00 at a Denver stadium.
    """
    hour = kickoff.instant.astimezone(ZoneInfo(game_zone)).hour
    if hour < 12:
        return "early"
    if hour < 18:
        return "afternoon"
    return "night"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TemplateEntry:
    """One obligation in a kickoff-band template, placed by offset from kickoff.

    ``start_at`` and ``end_at`` are ``"home"`` or ``"away"``; a travel leg has
    both. They become real IANA zones only when the template is applied to a
    specific game.
    """

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_at: str = "home"
    end_at: str | None = None
    movable: bool = False


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightMarker:
    """Curfew and wake-up for one night, as offsets from kickoff.

    Deliberately not an Event: event kinds are mandatory by default, so a
    curfew scheduled as an obligation would block the sleep it bounds.
    ``wake=None`` means the night has no wake-up call (Saturday, before the
    Sunday off day) and its end comes from the assumption set instead.
    """

    night: str
    curfew: timedelta
    wake: timedelta | None
    at: str = "home"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffBandTemplate:
    band: str
    game_type: str
    entries: tuple[TemplateEntry, ...]
    nights: tuple[NightMarker, ...]
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WindowOverride:
    """A staff-entered edge that replaces the rule's start, end, or both."""

    start: LocalTime | None = None
    end: LocalTime | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightPlan:
    """One night's proposed window, or ``None`` with the reason there is none."""

    night: str
    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""
    reporting: Interval | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from.

    The inputs are kept as entered, not re-derived from resolved instants: an
    override entered in Central time for a Mountain-time night, or one that
    leaves a night with no window, cannot be recovered from the result.
    """

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str
    nights: tuple[NightPlan, ...] = ()
    kickoff_entered: LocalTime | None = None
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] = field(default_factory=dict)
    extra_events: tuple[Event, ...] = ()


def _night_date(curfew: datetime, zone: str) -> date:
    local = curfew.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone))
    # A curfew before noon is already past midnight: it belongs to the night
    # that started the previous evening.
    return local.date() if local.hour >= 12 else local.date() - timedelta(days=1)


def _assumed_wake(night_date: date, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:
    if not assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "
            "saturday_night_wake; set an assumed wake time rather than leaving "
            "the night unbounded"
        )
    morning = night_date + timedelta(days=1)
    return LocalTime(f"{morning.isoformat()}T{assumptions.saturday_night_wake}", zone).instant


def _plan_night(
    marker: NightMarker,
    kickoff: datetime,
    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    curfew = kickoff + marker.curfew
    night_date = _night_date(curfew, zone)
    reporting = Interval.of(
        f"{night_date.isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_START}",
        f"{(night_date + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_END}",
        zone,
    )

    if marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = kickoff + marker.wake, "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(night_date, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    start, start_source = curfew, "curfew"
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < end:
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    window: ProtectedSleepWindow | None
    note: str = ""
    reporting: Interval | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GameWeekend:
    """A built weekend: the plain scenario plus what it was built from.

    The inputs are kept as entered, not re-derived from resolved instants: an
    override entered in Central time for a Mountain-time night, or one that
    leaves a night with no window, cannot be recovered from the result.
    """

    scenario: Scenario
    template: KickoffBandTemplate
    kickoff: datetime
    home_zone: str
    game_zone: str
    nights: tuple[NightPlan, ...] = ()
    kickoff_entered: LocalTime | None = None
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] = field(default_factory=dict)
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] = field(default_factory=dict)
    extra_events: tuple[Event, ...] = ()


def _night_date(curfew: datetime, zone: str) -> date:
    local = curfew.astimezone(ZoneInfo(zone))
    # A curfew before noon is already past midnight: it belongs to the night
    # that started the previous evening.
    return local.date() if local.hour >= 12 else local.date() - timedelta(days=1)


def _assumed_wake(night_date: date, zone: str, assumptions: AssumptionSet, night: str) -> datetime:
    if not assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{night} night has no wake-up call and the assumption set has no "
            "saturday_night_wake; set an assumed wake time rather than leaving "
            "the night unbounded"
        )
    morning = night_date + timedelta(days=1)
    return LocalTime(f"{morning.isoformat()}T{assumptions.saturday_night_wake}", zone).instant


def _plan_night(
    marker: NightMarker,
    kickoff: datetime,
    zone: str,
    obligations: list[Event],
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    override: WindowOverride | None,
) -> NightPlan:
    curfew = kickoff + marker.curfew
    night_date = _night_date(curfew, zone)
    reporting = Interval.of(
        f"{night_date.isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_START}",
        f"{(night_date + timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()}T{NIGHT_REPORT_END}",
        zone,
    )

    if marker.wake is not None:
        end, end_source = kickoff + marker.wake, "wake-up call"
    else:
        end, end_source = _assumed_wake(night_date, zone, assumptions, marker.night), "assumed wake"

    start, start_source = curfew, "curfew"
    for event in obligations:
        if event.interval.start < end:
            ready = event.interval.end + assumptions.pre_bed
            if ready > start:
                start, start_source = ready, f"obligation:{event.id}"

    if override is not None:
        if override.start is not None:
            start, start_source = override.start.instant, "staff override"
        if override.end is not None:
            end, end_source = override.end.instant, "staff override"

    if start >= end:
        return NightPlan(
            marker.night,
            None,
            note=f"no protected sleep window: {start_source} runs past the {end_source}",
            reporting=reporting,
        )

    window = ProtectedSleepWindow(
        id=f"{marker.night}-night",
        label=f"{marker.night.capitalize()} night",
        interval=Interval(start, end, start_zone=zone, end_zone=zone),
        kind="hotel" if marker.at == "away" else "home",
        proposed=True,
        start_source=start_source,
        end_source=end_source,
    )
    return NightPlan(marker.night, window, reporting=reporting)


def build_weekend(
    template: KickoffBandTemplate,
    kickoff: LocalTime,
    *,
    home_zone: str,
    game_zone: str,
    assumptions: AssumptionSet,
    id: str,
    title: str,
    offsets: Mapping[str, tuple[timedelta, timedelta]] | None = None,
    extra_events: Iterable[Event] = (),
    window_overrides: Mapping[str, WindowOverride] | None = None,
) -> GameWeekend:
    """Apply a template to one kickoff and propose each night's sleep window.

    ``offsets`` replaces an entry's (start, end) offsets; that is how a
    candidate moves Friday practice or meetings. ``extra_events`` are placed by
    clock time and do not move when kickoff does. ``window_overrides`` replaces
    a rule-proposed edge, keyed by night.
    """
    band = band_for(kickoff, game_zone)
    if band != template.band:
        raise ValueError(
            f"kickoff {kickoff.wall} {kickoff.zone} falls in the {band} band, "
            f"but template {template.source!r} is for the {template.band} band"
        )

    overrides = dict(offsets or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(overrides) - {entry.id for entry in template.entries})
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"offset override names no template entry: {', '.join(unknown)}")

    edges = dict(window_overrides or {})
    unknown_nights = sorted(set(edges) - {marker.night for marker in template.nights})
    if unknown_nights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"window override names no night in the template: {', '.join(unknown_nights)}"
        )

    extras = tuple(extra_events)
    zones = {"home": home_zone, "away": game_zone}
    instant = kickoff.instant
    events: list[Event] = []
    for entry in template.entries:
        start, end = overrides.get(entry.id, (entry.start, entry.end))
        anchor = KickoffAnchor(
            start, end, zones[entry.start_at], zones[entry.end_at or entry.start_at]
        )
        events.append(
            Event(
                id=entry.id,
                kind=entry.kind,
                title=entry.title,
                interval=anchor.resolve(instant),
                movable=entry.movable,
                anchor=anchor,
            )
        )
    events.extend(extras)

    obligations = [event for event in events if event.mandatory]
    nights = tuple(
        _plan_night(
            marker, instant, zones[marker.at], obligations, assumptions, edges.get(marker.night)
        )
        for marker in template.nights
    )

    scenario = Scenario(
        id=id,
        title=title,
        display_zone=home_zone,
        events=events,
        windows=[plan.window for plan in nights if plan.window is not None],
        assumptions=assumptions,
    )
    return GameWeekend(
        scenario=scenario,
        template=template,
        kickoff=instant,
        home_zone=home_zone,
        game_zone=game_zone,
        nights=nights,
        kickoff_entered=kickoff,
        offsets=overrides,
        window_overrides=edges,
        extra_events=extras,
    )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NightReport:
    night: str
    plan: NightPlan
    report: OpportunityReport

    @property
    def hours(self) -> float:
        return self.report.hours

    @property
    def note(self) -> str:
        return self.plan.note


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WeekendReport:
    weekend: GameWeekend
    nights: tuple[NightReport, ...]

    def night(self, name: str) -> NightReport:
        for report in self.nights:
            if report.night == name:
                return report
        raise KeyError(f"no {name!r} night in this weekend")


def evaluate_weekend(weekend: GameWeekend) -> WeekendReport:
    """Opportunity for each night, over that night's date-fixed interval."""
    return WeekendReport(
        weekend=weekend,
        nights=tuple(
            NightReport(plan.night, plan, evaluate(weekend.scenario, plan.reporting))
            for plan in weekend.nights
        ),
    )


def _signed(delta: timedelta) -> str:
    minutes = round(delta.total_seconds() / 60)
    sign = "+" if minutes >= 0 else "-"
    minutes = abs(minutes)
    return f"{sign}{minutes // 60}h{minutes % 60:02d}m"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class WeekendComparison:
    baseline: WeekendReport
    candidate: WeekendReport
    nights: tuple[tuple[str, Comparison], ...]
    changed_events: list[EventChange]
    kickoff_shift: timedelta

    def night(self, name: str) -> Comparison:
        for night, comparison in self.nights:
            if night == name:
                return comparison
        raise KeyError(f"no {name!r} night in this comparison")

    @property
    def fixed_event_changes(self) -> list[EventChange]:
        return [c for c in self.changed_events if not c.movable]

    @property
    def removed_events(self) -> list[str]:
        kept = {e.id for e in self.candidate.weekend.scenario.events}
        return [e.id for e in self.baseline.weekend.scenario.events if e.id not in kept]

    @property
    def added_events(self) -> list[str]:
        existing = {e.id for e in self.baseline.weekend.scenario.events}
        return [e.id for e in self.candidate.weekend.scenario.events if e.id not in existing]

    @property
    def flags(self) -> list[str]:
        """Plain-language warnings that the candidate changed something fixed.

        Flagged rather than refused: staff may legitimately explore a
        different kickoff, but nobody should win an argument by doing it
        quietly, and dropping an obligation is never a lever.
        """
        flags = []
        if self.kickoff_shift:
            flags.append(f"kickoff moved {_signed(self.kickoff_shift)}; kickoff is fixed, not a lever")
        for change in self.fixed_event_changes:
            flags.append(
                f"{change.event_id} changed (start {_signed(change.shift)}, "
                f"end {_signed(change.end_shift)}) but is not a movable event"
            )
        for event_id in self.removed_events:
            flags.append(
                f"{event_id} is missing from the candidate; dropping an obligation "
                "is not a lever"
            )
        return flags


def compare_weekends(baseline: GameWeekend, candidate: GameWeekend) -> WeekendComparison:
    """Night-by-night difference, plus what moved and whether it was allowed to."""
    before = evaluate_weekend(baseline)
    after = evaluate_weekend(candidate)
    names = [n.night for n in before.nights]
    if names != [n.night for n in after.nights]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"cannot compare weekends with different nights: {names} vs "
            f"{[n.night for n in after.nights]}"
        )
    return WeekendComparison(
        baseline=before,
        candidate=after,
        nights=tuple(
            (b.night, compare(b.report, a.report)) for b, a in zip(before.nights, after.nights)
        ),
        changed_events=event_changes(baseline.scenario, candidate.scenario),
        kickoff_shift=candidate.kickoff - baseline.kickoff,
    )

"""The Friday early-kickoff comparison: the first complete Release 1 workflow.

Runs against the synthetic game-weekend fixtures in ``fixtures/``: an early
road kickoff where Friday meetings run 22:00-23:00 MT in the baseline and an
hour earlier in the candidate. The assertions that matter most are the negative
ones: the report must never print a fatigue or effectiveness number, and must
never describe opportunity as sleep obtained.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path

from sleep_scheduler.cli import main, render_weekend_comparison
from sleep_scheduler.persistence import load_weekend, save_scenario
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import compare_weekends

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures"
BASELINE = FIXTURES / "friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json"
CANDIDATE = FIXTURES / "friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json"


def fixture_comparison():
    return compare_weekends(load_weekend(BASELINE), load_weekend(CANDIDATE))


def rendered():
    return render_weekend_comparison(fixture_comparison())


# --- What the fixture shows -----------------------------------------------------


def test_moving_friday_meetings_earlier_gains_thirty_minutes_on_friday_night():
    assert fixture_comparison().night("fri").hours_delta == 0.5


def test_the_friday_decision_leaves_thursday_and_saturday_unchanged():
    comparison = fixture_comparison()
    assert (comparison.night("thu").hours_delta, comparison.night("sat").hours_delta) == (0.0, 0.0)


def test_fixture_candidate_moves_only_a_lever():
    comparison = fixture_comparison()
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.changed_events] == ["fri-meeting"]
    assert comparison.flags == []


def test_baseline_friday_falls_short_of_the_assumed_target():
    assert fixture_comparison().night("fri").baseline.shortfall_hours > 0


# --- Report wording ---------------------------------------------------------------


def test_rendered_report_labels_the_measure_as_opportunity():
    assert "sleep opportunity" in rendered().lower()


FORECAST_TERMS = ("effectiveness", "fatigue", "predicted sleep", "sleep obtained", "readiness")
NEGATIONS = ("no ", "not ", "unavailable", "cannot", "carry no")


def test_forecast_terms_appear_only_inside_an_explicit_denial():
    # These words are allowed in a sentence that says the value is unavailable,
    # and nowhere else. A line stating one as a result would fail here.
    for line in rendered().lower().splitlines():
        if any(term in line for term in FORECAST_TERMS):
            assert any(marker in line for marker in NEGATIONS), (
                f"line states a forecast term as a result: {line!r}"
            )


def test_report_opens_by_disclaiming_that_opportunity_is_sleep_obtained():
    first_line = rendered().splitlines()[0].lower()
    assert "sleep opportunity" in first_line
    assert "not sleep obtained" in first_line


def night_rows(text):
    return [
        line for line in text.lower().splitlines()
        if line.strip().startswith(("thu", "fri", "sat")) and "h " in line

Runs against the synthetic fixtures in ``fixtures/``. The assertions that matter
most are the negative ones: the report must never print a fatigue or
effectiveness number, and must never describe opportunity as sleep obtained.
"""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.cli import main, render_comparison
from sleep_scheduler.opportunity import compare, evaluate
from sleep_scheduler.persistence import load_scenario
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures"
CHICAGO = "America/Chicago"
OVERNIGHT = Interval.of("2026-09-12T18:00", "2026-09-13T12:00", CHICAGO)


def fixture_comparison():
    baseline = evaluate(load_scenario(FIXTURES / "late-return-baseline.json"), OVERNIGHT)
    candidate = evaluate(load_scenario(FIXTURES / "late-return-candidate.json"), OVERNIGHT)
    return compare(baseline, candidate)


def test_moving_the_morning_lift_later_increases_opportunity():
    delta = fixture_comparison()
    assert delta.hours_delta > 0


def test_baseline_fixture_falls_short_of_the_assumed_target():
    delta = fixture_comparison()
    assert delta.baseline.shortfall_hours > 0


def test_rendered_report_labels_the_measure_as_opportunity():
    assert "sleep opportunity" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()


FORECAST_TERMS = ("effectiveness", "fatigue", "predicted sleep", "sleep obtained", "readiness")
NEGATIONS = ("no ", "not ", "unavailable", "cannot", "carry no")


def test_forecast_terms_appear_only_inside_an_explicit_denial():
    # These words are allowed in a sentence that says the value is unavailable,

        if any(term in line for term in FORECAST_TERMS):
            assert any(marker in line for marker in NEGATIONS), (
                f"line states a forecast term as a result: {line!r}"
            )

    first_line = render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).splitlines()[0].lower()
    assert "sleep opportunity" in first_line
    assert "not sleep obtained" in first_line


def test_numeric_result_rows_carry_no_forecast_terms():
    # The rows a reader takes numbers from must be opportunity-only.
    text = render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()
    rows = [l for l in text.splitlines() if "h " in l and ("late return" in l or "difference" in l)]
    assert rows, "expected the comparison table to have result rows"
    for row in rows:
        for forbidden in FORECAST_TERMS:
            assert forbidden not in row, f"result row must not mention {forbidden!r}: {row!r}"


def test_rendered_report_names_the_target_source():
    assert "staff default" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison())

    assert "unavailable" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()


def test_rendered_report_lists_the_event_that_moved():
    assert "lift" in render_comparison(fixture_comparison()).lower()

    code = main(
        [
            str(FIXTURES / "late-return-baseline.json"),
            str(FIXTURES / "late-return-candidate.json"),
        ]
    )
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert code == 0
    assert "sleep opportunity" in out.lower()


def shift_to_next_year(name: str, tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Same fixture, different dates, so a hardcoded window cannot match it."""
    import json

    payload = json.loads((FIXTURES / name).read_text())
    for group in ("events", "windows"):
        for item in payload[group]:
            for edge in ("start", "end"):
                item["interval"][edge] = item["interval"][edge].replace("2026-09-1", "2027-04-1")
    path = tmp_path / name
    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload))
    return path

    assert "0h 00m" not in capsys.readouterr().out.split("Target:")[0]

            "--window",

            "2026-09-13T12:00",
            "America/Chicago",

    )

    assert "0h 00m" in capsys.readouterr().out
